Aggregate polygon-level values up to a different, arbitrary polygon layer

Source: R/aggregate_values_to_polygons.R
mysterymaps_aggregate_values_to_polygons.Rd

Used when a target geography is not the same as the source geography (e.g. rolling county-level values up to Hospital Referral Regions, which do not nest inside standard Census geographies). Each source polygon is reduced to an interior point (sf::st_point_on_surface()) and assigned to whichever target polygon contains it; values are then summed per target.

Usage

mysterymaps_aggregate_values_to_polygons(
  source_poly,
  source_values,
  target_poly,
  value_col = "n"
)

Arguments

source_poly

sf polygons with an id column (e.g. counties).

source_values

data.frame with columns id and value_col.

target_poly

sf polygons with an id column (e.g. HRRs).

value_col

character(1): name of the value column to sum. Default "n".

Value

A tibble with columns id (the target id) and value_col (summed).

Details

This is an approximation for a source polygon that straddles a target boundary: it is assigned whole to one target rather than split proportionally by area, so a source value near a target boundary can land on either side depending on where its interior point happens to fall.

See also

Other mapping: mysterymaps_access_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_access_choropleth_map_multi(), mysterymaps_accessibility_map(), mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_cartogram_map(), mysterymaps_catchment_redundancy_map(), mysterymaps_choropleth_point_map(), mysterymaps_clear_isochrone_cache(), mysterymaps_count_points_in_polygons(), mysterymaps_create_isochrones(), mysterymaps_flow_map(), mysterymaps_hrr_maps(), mysterymaps_isochrones_for_df(), mysterymaps_jitter_points(), mysterymaps_map_acceptance_rate(), mysterymaps_map_acog_districts(), mysterymaps_map_base(), mysterymaps_map_block_group(), mysterymaps_map_leaflet(), mysterymaps_map_physicians(), mysterymaps_pathway_small_multiples_map(), mysterymaps_plot_isochrones(), mysterymaps_rate_choropleth_map(), mysterymaps_scale_bar()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
counties <- sf::st_sf(
  id = 1:2,
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-100, -98, -98, -100, -100), c(39, 39, 41, 41, 39)))),
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-98, -96, -96, -98, -98), c(39, 39, 41, 41, 39)))),
    crs = 4326))
regions <- sf::st_sf(
  id = "R1",
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(-101, -95, -95, -101, -101), c(38, 38, 42, 42, 38)))),
    crs = 4326))
mysterymaps_aggregate_values_to_polygons(
  counties, data.frame(id = 1:2, n = c(3, 4)), regions, value_col = "n")
}
